newsitem.title: CANADA: Alcan says to sue British Columbia.
newsitem.headline: Alcan says to sue British Columbia.

text.p: Alcan Aluminium Ltd said on Monday it will sue the Canadian province of British Columbia for compensation over its cancelled Kemano hydroelectric project after concluding that a negotiated settlement is not possible.
The provincial government and Alcan have negotiated unsuccessfully for two years after the province in 1995 ordered the cancellation of the half-built Kemano project.
Alcan spent C$535 million on the project in northern British Columbia which was intended to provide power to Alcan's Kitimat smelter.
"We have concluded that a negotiated settlement is not possible, and have therefore decided to put the matter before the courts," Alcan chief executive Jacques Bougie said.

Alcan filed with the court in January but said this was only a precautionary move intended to protect its right to sue later if talks failed. After not talking for several months, the two sides resumed negotiations in March with the goal of reaching a deal in two months.
But the company said Monday it found itself "going backward rather than forward with this process" and served the province with a writ of summons and statement of claim.
Despite saying Alcan was convinced talks were fruitless, the company said it was "prepared to sit down with the government at any time to discuss out-of-court options."

Bougie said Alcan would reinvest in British Columbia any compensation awarded by the courts and would continue to consider the province as a location for potential expansion, "as long as the Province accepts referring this matter to the courts and agrees to live by the agreements and working relationship developed over the past 45 years between Alcan and B.C."
